teams.synopsis: Undefeated, and most points for in the league by 22 - easily #1 for a third straight week.
teams.blurb: Undefeated. Most PF by 22. Yeah, this team is easily ranked 1st once again for the third week in a row. With a light matchup in Week 5, where Grits is favored by 25.5 points, I expect the team to move to 5-0 and continue their dominance. The real challenge should come in Week 6 against MFGA. Current record: 4-0. Projected: 12-2.

teams.synopsis: The best start in franchise history, undefeated through the first month - a 5-0 week sets up a huge Week 6.
teams.blurb: MFGA is off to the best start in franchise history, undefeated through the first month of the 2025 season. Week 5 could be tricky without the QB2, RB4, and WR17, but they face one of the league's worst teams. A 5-0 win sets up a treat in Week 6 against the top-ranked team. Current record: 4-0. Projected: 10-4.

teams.synopsis: One of the most consistent teams in the PFFL, never scoring under 116 in a week - Week 5 tests the depth.
teams.blurb: One of the most consistent teams in the PFFL, Shakir to Death has never scored under 116 points in a week. Week 5 will be their biggest test, not because the matchup is tough but because they'll be without Kraft and Swift. Still, I could see the team overperforming and winning. Current record: 2-2. Projected: 10-4.

teams.synopsis: Could be higher, but a top-three team has to falter first - no complaints about this roster.
teams.blurb: LP could be higher, but until a top-three team falters, 4th will have to do. I have no complaints about this roster. Week 2 looked like a fluke, and their true form shows in Week 5, projected for the second-most points. They're expected to win games, but I could see even more. Current record: 3-1. Projected: 10-4.

teams.synopsis: Staying put at 5th for the second straight week, though a poor Week 5 projection could change that fast.
teams.blurb: I'll keep myself at 5th for the second straight week, but that could very likely change after Week 5, due to a poor projection and a tough matchup against the league's top team. The RBs are still weak, as Henderson has yet to take a jump, so a trade might be necessary at some point. Current record: 3-1. Projected: 7-7.

teams.synopsis: Recently labeled a fraud by league members, but still a top-6 team heading into Week 5.
teams.blurb: Recently labeled a fraud by PFFL members, Gibbayyyyyyyy remains a top-6 team heading into Week 5. The squad has the fourth-lowest PF and the fewest PA, but that's fantasy football. A rank drop could come if Ladd doesn't step up, yet for now, they're expected to stay competitive. Current record: 3-1. Projected: 7-7.

teams.synopsis: The top-ranked 1-3 team - a healthy Kittle could make this roster dangerous fast.
teams.blurb: Here it is, the top-ranked 1-3 team. I like LCU's roster, especially if Kittle returns to top form after his hamstring injury. Like the other 1-3 teams, Week 5 will be crucial for a win to avoid being backed into a corner. Current record: 1-3. Projected: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: A massive pre-Week-5 trade netted a top RB and fine WRs - Jacobs on bye is the only real concern.
teams.blurb: A massive trade prior to Week 5 netted the Minutemen a top RB and some fine WRs, but with Jacobs on a bye in Week 5, will the team have enough to avoid going 1-4? Lucky for them, they matchup against one of the bottom teams in the league, so despite the lack of an RB1 they can still secure a win. Current record: 1-3. Projected: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: Maybe too high on this team, but the pieces for a competitive squad are there - the schedule is the real obstacle.
teams.blurb: Woah. Maybe I'm a bit high on this team, but I don't care. The pieces for a competitive squad are there; the schedule, especially a tough Week 5, is the main obstacle. Like NY, this team could rebound in the second half, but only time will tell. Current record: 1-3. Projected: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: 1-3 isn't ideal, but NY avoids both 4-0 teams the rest of the season - room for a real turnaround.
teams.blurb: Being 1-3 isn't ideal, but NY avoids both 4-0 teams for the rest of the season. The schedule sets up potential for a turnaround. The team could keep climbing, but a lot depends on their Week 5 matchup against another 1-3 squad. Current record: 1-3. Projected: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: Tricky to rank after injuries and setbacks, but there's clear promise - a 2-2 record some call lucky.
teams.blurb: Harvey is tricky to rank. The team has been shaken by injuries and setbacks, yet there's clear promise and potential. Some call their 2-2 record lucky, but if that's true, it gives them room to stumble without being in immediate danger of missing the playoffs. Current record: 2-2. Projected: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: One of seven teams sitting at 1-3, with a winnable Week 5 matchup to make a real statement.
teams.blurb: Could the team be higher? Maybe, but until more production like the team had in Week 4 is shown, then 12th seems fair. These next couple weeks will be very telling, especially with a winnable matchup in Week 5. RWB is one of 7 teams to be 1-3 - will they rise to the occasion? Current record: 1-3. Projected: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: Tyreek Hill's injury leaves Jameson Williams as the acting WR1 - a tough fall from the top of the league.
teams.blurb: LDT takes a hit in Week 4 as Tyreek Hill goes down, leaving Jameson Williams as the acting WR1. It's tough to watch this team fall from grace after starting the season at the top of the league. Still, the pieces remain to make a big impact. A trade should be expected soon to get the WR room in order. Current record: 1-3. Projected: 4-10.

teams.synopsis: Nabers is out for the season and the RB room is thin - a loss here could kick off a rough stretch.
teams.blurb: Welp. Nabers is out for the season and RB depth is thin. TTF doesn't have much room to fall, but Week 5 brings a matchup against a 4-0 team hit by byes and injuries. A win could reveal what this team can really do, but a loss could kick start a trip to McDonald's. Current record: 1-3. Projected: 2-12.
